text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.5% today as oil prices spiked on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran has escalated tanker attacks, and the Trump administration announced new sanctions on Iranian "shadow fleet" vessels while reportedly considering large-scale military operations in Iran — the kind of disruption that can constrain global oil supply and push prices higher. With world oil trading at $125 a barrel (up sharply from earlier in the week), an oil producer like ConocoPhillips benefits directly from the higher price it can sell crude at.

The stock's broader two-week gain of 4% also reflects a tightening energy market. Refinery capacity constraints and political pressure on fuel prices are keeping downstream margins under pressure, but for upstream producers focused on crude extraction rather than refining, the sharp oil price environment is a tailwind.
